worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 45,000.00 = 45,000.00. Federal taxable income = 45,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 1 x 1,600.00 additional for age 65 or older = 11,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 45,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 33,100.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 low- and middle-income worksheet: line 1 45,000.00; line 2 30,000.00; line 3 15,000.00; line 4 0.10; line 5 1,500.00; line 6 2,500.00 - 1,500.00 = 1,000.00; line 7 2 exemption(s); line 8 = 2,000.00. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (married filing jointly) row for federal AGI 45,000.00 gives 3,000.00 x 1 qualifying = 3,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 3,000.00. Line 17 = 45,000.00 + 0.00 - 33,100.00 - 2,000.00 - 3,000.00 = 6,900.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 11,900.00 = 11,900.00; less base deductions 5,000.00 gives 6,900.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 6,900.00 = 103.5; total 103.5, to the cent 103.50. The table row over 6,800 to 6,900 gives 103; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 103.50. Only the spouse aged 66 qualifies: one amount, not two. Row 42,001 to 45,000.
